Solid chord reference database.. This app has no ads. It has major, minor, minor and major 7th, aug, and dim chords for all twelve tones, correct standard voicings in two variations. It has a plethora of other chord voicings ranging from standard to useable, and every one I can at least see how the author reasoned it out. None are wrong. I don’t know what more one could reasonably ask for in a free app. It’s more than I would have. Much gratitude for the author, who took their time to make a completely free, good looking, and easily navigable chord reference database that will be a boon for the beginner, the intermediate, and the veteran.

Intuitive and helpful. Very straight forward & intuitive. Sure, it could have a few extra simple features, but that’s not what this app is about.

There’s a million other chord apps with all sorts of extra options and stuff but those apps all cost money, (usually a subscription based payment system which is the worst!), and the free ones are invariably littered with obnoxious ads that pop up every 10 seconds.

With this app you will not see any advertisements, you will not be asked for any money, and it does everything the App Store says it does. Nothing more. Nothing less. It LITERALLY could not be any more straight forward than that.

If there’s a person who owns this app but doesn’t understand how it works, I would want to know how that person managed to download the app in the first place, or how they were able to unlock their own iPhone/iPad, (and then I’d wonder if that person even knows what a guitar chord is, because…well, you get the idea.)

Very useful, easy to use. This a great little tool, especially for beginners, even more especially those seeking to progress to the more ‘exotic’ chords. Beautifully simple, you just select the root note and then the type of chord (e.g. ‘C’ and then ‘Maj7’ and it will give you a couple of diagrams, giving you different voicings of the chord. Also has an option for lefties (I’ve not tried it, don’t need to, but good that the app maker thought of that - don’t often see left-handed diagrams in tab sheets). Only thing I’d ask is for is some ‘add’ chords, although the maker says he’ll be adding more in time. 
Cheers!
